answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks when identity costs something the attacker cannot fake. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, slashed on a failed audit. The quill of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The opal is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the sable.
